about.title: Alameda Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Alameda is an island city, and word travels quickly when someone is lost here. In 2025, the city recorded 129 injury collisions, 166 people hurt, and one traffic death — a small figure on paper, and an enormous one for the family living it. Fatal crashes are only part of the picture, though. A wrongful death claim in Alameda County can follow a collision on Lincoln Avenue or Park Street, a fall on someone else's property, a medical error, or an unsafe product. What ties these together is a death that might have been avoided had someone used reasonable care. California treats wrongful death as a civil matter, entirely separate from any criminal charges the district attorney may or may not bring. The right to file belongs to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then to certain dependents and heirs. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Alameda families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Alameda Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out your family's situation before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be brought within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected promptly protects those dates.

items.title: The full measure of loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Your attorney's job is to make sure none of that is overlooked.

items.question: The crash on Central Avenue is still under police investigation. Do we have to wait for the criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, regardless of whether prosecutors ever file charges. The two-year clock runs from the date of death either way, so waiting for the criminal process to finish can cost valuable time. An attorney can begin gathering evidence while the investigation continues.

items.question: Who in our family is actually allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California puts the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children first in line. If there are none, certain dependents and heirs may have standing. Because families are rarely simple, an attorney will look at your specific circumstances rather than assume.

items.question: What kinds of losses can be included in an Alameda wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Funeral and burial expenses are part of it, as is the financial support your loved one would have provided over time. California also recognizes the loss of love, companionship, and guidance, which is often the heaviest loss of all. No attorney can promise a result, but they can make sure each category is properly documented and presented.
